verdicts.reason: The mechanical core is real and I reproduced it: with GATE_TOOLS_DIR pointed at a scratch cache holding a planted `actionlint-1.7.12/actionlint` and `zizmor-1.29.0/venv/bin/zizmor`, ensure_actionlint() and ensure_zizmor() both returned 0 with the note 'reusing the cache', set the BIN variables to the planted files, executed them, and compared zero SHA-256 values; the cache hit even outranks a legitimate actionlint of the pinned version sitting in PATH, because line 110 is tested before line 116. The privilege-crossing half is narrower than stated: no host where a second principal can write that path was named or observed.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-01 (compensating control): fails — I read lines 25-28 and 168 and confirmed the SHA-256 comparison is downstream of the two early `return 0`s, so no control guards the cache branch; the file header's claim that the pin is 'the equivalent of the SHA pin we demand from actions' is false on that branch. FP-02 (value not attacker-controlled): fails — the cache name is a fixed literal, not generated, and `mkdir -p` at 72/139 never checks ownership or mode. FP-04 (path does not ship): fails — .github/README-governance.md:99-102 documents `scripts/gates/run-all.sh` as the local command, and nothing there sets GATE_TOOLS_DIR. FP-06 (no second principal): HOLDS for every invocation anyone can point at — ci.yml:121, supply-chain-audit.yml:49 and release.yml:414 all override GATE_TOOLS_DIR to ${{ runner.temp }} on an ephemeral single-tenant ubuntu-latest runner, and I measured on this macOS host that TMPDIR is a per-user 0700 Darwin directory (and that bare `mktemp` uses it even when TMPDIR is overridden). It DOES_NOT_HOLD only on a Linux host with TMPDIR unset plus a second local account, which remains unobserved exactly as the finding admits.
verdicts.severity_assessment: overstated — `high` is not supportable for the exploit path: every invocation the repository actually makes is immune, and the exposed configuration is a deployment nobody has seen. `medium` is the honest rating. In the other direction one half is understated: that a cache hit is executed without ever comparing the pinned SHA-256 needs NO precondition at all — it is true on the maintainer's own Mac and in CI on every second and later run — and that unconditional integrity defect is buried inside a `probable` exploit narrative instead of standing on its own.
verdicts.checked: Read scripts/gates/lib/bootstrap-actions-lint.sh in full and scripts/gates/gate-actions-lint.sh in full (call sites at 96 and 127); grepped GATE_TOOLS_DIR across the whole target (6 hits, 3 of them workflow overrides); read scripts/gates/run-all.sh in full and scripts/gates/lib/common.sh in full; read .github/README-governance.md §3 for the documented local command; confirmed the contrast citation at gate-plugin-integrity.sh:137 verbatim. Executed a COPY of the bootstrap in a scratch directory with PATH stripped of curl and gh so no download was possible, and captured that the planted binaries ran and that BOOTSTRAP_NOTES contained zero 'SHA-256 verified' lines. Measured mktemp/TMPDIR behaviour on Darwin.
verdicts.not_checked: Whether the four pinned SHA-256 constants match the upstream rhysd/actionlint 1.7.12 checksums (no network). Whether any real maintainer host has an unset TMPDIR and a second local account. The symlink variants at lines 153 and 173 were read but not exercised. No Linux host was available to confirm /tmp mode 1777 behaviour empirically.

verdicts.reason: The chain is real and I reproduced every link of the mechanism on Python 3.12.10: `python3 -c`, a heredoc on stdin, and `python3 -` all set sys.path[0] to the current working directory, and a yaml.py or json.py in that directory is imported and its top-level code executed in place of PyYAML and of the stdlib. release.yml:409 sets `working-directory: source`, run-all.sh:192 launches each gate with `bash "$g"` and never changes directory, and gate-labels-taxonomy.sh:31/44, gate-plugin-integrity.sh:410 and gate-bench-integrity.sh:34 all hand Python a script that is not a file in the gates directory. What is narrower than stated is the impact.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-01 (compensating control): fails — I read release.yml:393-406 and the `cmp -s` proof covers run-all.sh and lib/common.sh as FILES; nothing in it touches the interpreter search path, and the replacement is of source/scripts/gates, not of the candidate's root. FP-04 (path does not ship): fails — verify is the job whose exit code gates promotion (release.yml:418-425). FP-06 (no second principal): fails in the local variant — README-governance.md:99 documents running run-all.sh from a tree's root, and a contributor's branch is a second principal; in the CI variant the principal must first land the file on main's first-parent chain, which I read at release.yml:245-267. FP-09 (construct is not what it looks like): fails — I ran all three constructs and each shadowed as claimed, including the `-c` form. I also looked for a gate that would reject a root-level .py: gate-plugin-integrity.sh:350 scopes its extension allowlist to EHS_SERVED_ROOTS (skills agents commands hooks) and gate-tree-delta.sh:35 to skills agents, so nothing stops the file, exactly as the finding says.
verdicts.severity_assessment: agree with `medium`, but the IMPACT sentence is overstated and should be corrected. 'content published to the stable branch and tag that no gate saw' is wrong: the promote job still runs gate-plugin-version.sh and gate-plugin-integrity.sh from tools/ (release.yml:582 and 587) with cwd = the workspace root, which contains only tools/ and source/ and is therefore NOT shadowable, plus the `git diff` tree gate at 553-575 and `claude plugin tag --dry-run` at 597. Four independent checks still see the tree; what the finding actually defeats is the full suite in verify. Two preconditions also compound rather than one: the attacker must hold merge rights on main AND main's tip must have been cleaned up afterwards, since tools/ is the tip of main and would otherwise be the attacker's own code too.
verdicts.checked: Read .github/workflows/release.yml in full (resolve, verify and promote), scripts/gates/run-all.sh in full, scripts/gates/gate-labels-taxonomy.sh:1-70, gate-plugin-integrity.sh:130-200 and 395-420, gate-bench-integrity.sh:20-60, .github/workflows/ci.yml in full, .github/README-governance.md §3 and §4. Ran a scratch-directory harness exercising all four Python invocation forms with hostile yaml.py and json.py present, plus PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 as the control, which restored the stdlib module.
verdicts.not_checked: No candidate commit carrying such a module exists, so the end-to-end promotion was not exercised. I did not enumerate every module every inline Python block imports (only yaml and json were tested). I did not verify that a hostile module could actually rewrite run-all.sh's RESULTS file or the not-yet-run gate scripts — that step of the escalation is argued, not demonstrated. The `promote` job's own gates were read but not run.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism holds and I reproduced it: a script created in a directory and executed BY PATH puts that directory at sys.path[0], and a yaml.py planted beside it is imported and its top-level code executed instead of site-packages PyYAML — I ran the exact body of apply-governance.sh:554-569 and watched the hostile module run. But the finding's own evidence sentence is wrong for the only platform the script targets, which narrows the exposure sharply.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-06 (no second principal): this is where the finding gives ground. The evidence says '`mktemp` with no template creates the file inside ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}'. I measured it on Darwin and bare `mktemp` does NOT honour TMPDIR at all: with TMPDIR forced to a scratch path it still produced /var/folders/34/.../T/tmp.XXXXXXXX, the per-user 0700 Darwin directory. The script declares itself macOS-only in its own text (line 40 'bash 3.2, the only one macOS ships'; line 147 'this Mac'), so on its target platform there is no shared directory and no second principal by construction, not merely by accident. FP-01 (compensating control): fails — the invocation at 570 has no PYTHONSAFEPATH, no -P, no cd. FP-04 (path does not ship): fails on Linux — lines 543-547 gate only on ci.yml existing and python3 being present, both normal. FP-08: the live host configuration is not an artifact anyone produced, so UNKNOWN was the right answer. Net: the finding survives on a GNU/Linux host (GNU mktemp does use TMPDIR then /tmp) but is refuted for macOS, and macOS is the only deployment the file itself describes.
verdicts.severity_assessment: overstated. `high` is defended by the impact (code execution inside a process holding an admin gh session), but severity in this vocabulary is impact in THIS system, and the reachable population is a deployment nobody has observed while the platform the script names is immune by construction. The script is also invoked by no workflow in .github/workflows, so it only ever runs when a maintainer runs it by hand. `medium` at the very most; `low` is defensible. It is also worth recording that the finding's factual claim about mktemp and TMPDIR is simply incorrect on macOS and should be rewritten rather than restated.
verdicts.checked: Read scripts/gh/apply-governance.sh lines 1-60, 130-175, 215-240, 270-365 and 535-600; confirmed every cited line number (550, 554, 570, 143, 160, 147) is exactly where the finding says. Ran a scratch harness reproducing the by-path execution with a hostile yaml.py in the script's directory (module executed, yaml resolved to the planted file). Measured `mktemp` against TMPDIR on this Darwin host, both with an override and with TMPDIR unset.
verdicts.not_checked: GNU coreutils mktemp behaviour was not exercised (no Linux host available); the TMPDIR-honouring claim for Linux rests on documented behaviour. The other mktemp uses at 201, 388, 417, 433 and 509 were not re-traced — I took the finding's word that they are `gh --input` payloads. Whether the maintainer ever runs this script on a multi-user host is unknowable from the artifacts.

verdicts.reason: Read end to end and reproduced inertly. `FAILURES` occurs exactly once in gate-actions-lint.sh (line 92); the exit status is RC_FINAL, changed only by escalate() at 43, and escalate is not called in that branch. I ran the verbatim control flow of lines 86-93 against a scratch tree containing nested/.github/workflows/evil.yml: it printed the FAIL line, set FAILURES=1, and the simulated process exited 0. There is no gate-actions-lint.selftest.sh, so ci.yml:73's negative battery does not cover this gate.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-01 (compensating control): fails — gate_fail() in lib/common.sh:34 only printf's; nothing reads FAILURES; no trap, no ERR handler, no `set -e` (the file is `set -uo pipefail`). FP-09 (construct is not what it looks like): fails — I checked whether `gate_fail` might set a status through a side effect and it does not. FP-10 (bounded to informational): HOLDS, and I agree with the specialist's own answer: GitHub executes workflows only from .github/workflows at the repository root, so a stray file at another path is not executable content. I additionally found a narrowing the finding did NOT report, which strengthens rather than weakens it: the whole stray block sits inside `if ensure_zizmor; then`, so on any host where zizmor cannot be installed the check never runs at all.
verdicts.severity_assessment: agree — `informational` severity and `hardening` status are both correct. There is a documented guarantee that is not implemented, and nothing exploitable escapes through it. Do not let anyone inflate this one on the strength of the word FAIL appearing in a green log.
verdicts.checked: Read scripts/gates/gate-actions-lint.sh in full and scripts/gates/lib/common.sh in full; grepped FAILURES across the file; listed scripts/gates/ and confirmed the absence of gate-actions-lint.selftest.sh; read ci.yml:68-92 to confirm the selftest battery is discovered by glob over *.selftest.sh. Ran a scratch simulation of lines 41-93 with a planted stray workflow and captured exit code 0.
verdicts.not_checked: I did not execute the real gate (that would install zizmor and actionlint over the network). I did not confirm against GitHub documentation that no workflow outside .github/workflows can execute — I accepted that platform fact, which is the load-bearing assumption of the FP-10 downgrade. Composite action.yml files elsewhere in the tree remain unexamined, as the finding's own limits say.

verdicts.reason: The in-repository mismatch is exactly as described and I read every link: governance.json declares promotion.required_contexts as ['gates','workflow-hardening'] (72-75) while branches.main.protection.required_status_checks.checks holds only {'context':'gates'} (113-119); desired_protection() at 281-290 builds the API payload from that array alone; verify_contexts_observed() is fed want_ctx derived from the same payload (line 352), so the second context is never validated as required; and release.yml contains no occurrence of check-run, conclusion or status_checks anywhere. But the impact statement is wrong in a specific, checkable way.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-08 (control outside the repository): correctly UNKNOWN — no export of live branch protection exists, and governance.json says of itself 'This file does not apply itself'. FP-01 (compensating control): partly HOLDS and the finding under-weights it. Its impact claims 'the only detector this repository has for INF-14, for impostor commits and for known-vulnerable actions sits in the job that branch protection does not require'. Impostor-commit and known-vulnerable-actions are NOT run in that job: gate-actions-lint.sh:74-78 disables zizmor's online audits unless ZIZMOR_ONLINE=1 and a token are present, and ci.yml:115-122 sets neither. Those two audits run only in supply-chain-audit.yml:50-53, which is also not a required check. So requiring `workflow-hardening` would not have covered them, and what genuinely sits only in the unrequired job is zizmor's offline set (template-injection, dangerous-triggers, excessive-permissions, unpinned-uses, artipacked) plus actionlint and shellcheck. FP-06 (no second principal): pressure the finding does not acknowledge — the acting party is someone with write permission, and `enforce_admins: false` (governance.json:121) means required status checks do not bind the only actor observed to hold it anyway.
verdicts.severity_assessment: agree with `low`, and the title needs correcting rather than the rating. 'neither a required status check on main nor verified at promotion time' is contradicted by the finding's own limits: release.yml's verify job re-executes the whole suite including gate-actions-lint.sh over the candidate tree and refuses to promote on 1 or 2, so the stable channel IS covered, by re-execution rather than by asserting a check-run conclusion. The real residual gap is `latest` only, and its actor is a maintainer merging with a red check, not an attacker.
verdicts.checked: Read scripts/gh/governance.json in full; scripts/gh/apply-governance.sh lines 215-240, 270-365 and 535-600; .github/workflows/ci.yml in full; .github/workflows/supply-chain-audit.yml in full; scripts/gates/gate-actions-lint.sh:69-96 for the online-audit condition; scripts/gates/gate-workflow-hardening.sh:173-176 for its declared out-of-scope line; grepped release.yml for check-run/conclusion/status_checks (zero hits).
verdicts.not_checked: The live branch protection on GitHub — no API call was made, so the declared/actual relationship is unresolved in both directions. Whether an organization or account-level ruleset adds the second context. Whether any non-admin collaborator with write permission exists. Whether GitHub's auto-merge would in fact merge with a non-required check red (documented behaviour, not tested).

verdicts.reason: Every code fact checks out on a full read: `npm install -g "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}"` at release.yml:381 (verify) and 458 (promote), the version pinned in env at line 85, no --ignore-scripts, no lockfile and no package.json anywhere in the two directories provided, the promote job holding contents:write at 435, and the ordering exactly as claimed: tools/ checkout 446, setup-node 452, npm install 458, credentialed checkout 467, build 472, judging gates 582 and 587, push 646. Every line citation was accurate. What is not established, by the specialist or by me, is the half the impact depends on.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-05 (exposure intended and bounded): partly HOLDS and deserves to be recorded. The top-level version is pinned to an exact immutable release, and npm forbids republishing a version, so the named package's own code is not floating; the pin is materially stronger than the finding's framing of 'unpinned' suggests, and the only unpinned surface is the transitive closure. FP-01 (compensating control): fails — nothing verifies the install, and every other external dependency in the repo is digest-pinned (actions by 40-hex SHA, actionlint by SHA-256), so the inconsistency the finding rests on is real. FP-04 (path does not ship): fails — promote is the publishing job. FP-02 (value not attacker-controlled): I could not resolve the dependency tree offline, so I cannot say whether that closure is large, small or empty, nor whether it contains lifecycle scripts. Neither the specialist nor I measured it.
verdicts.severity_assessment: agree with `medium`. It matches the vocabulary's own definition — it requires chaining with a second issue that is not itself demonstrated (a compromised package) — and the finding is honest that no compromise is claimed. I would not raise it on the strength of the blast radius alone, and I would not lower it either: the ordering comment at 460-464 proves the authors already reasoned about this window and stopped one step short.
verdicts.checked: Read .github/workflows/release.yml in full, both install sites and the full promote job; verified the absence of any package.json, package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json under the target; cross-read scripts/gates/lib/bootstrap-actions-lint.sh:25-28 and 168 to confirm the digest-pinning contrast the finding draws.
verdicts.not_checked: The transitive dependency tree of @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.221 — its size, and whether it or the package itself declares preinstall/install/postinstall scripts — could not be resolved without network access. Whether `--ignore-scripts` would leave `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin tag --dry-run` working was not tested. npm's default lifecycle-script execution is documented behaviour I accepted rather than observed.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with a copy of the scanner over a synthetic tree. The same fabricated AKIA-format string was reported in clean.env but silently dropped from with_marker.env ('https://s3.example.com' later on the line), from with_marker2.md ('For example,' at the start of the line) and from a line carrying a PRIVATE KEY header plus the word 'example' — the suppression at line 84 tests the whole LINE, not m.group(0). A 2.4 MB file containing the same string and an undecodable binary file were both counted in the summary 'measured: 6 file(s)' while scan() returned [] for them at lines 72 and 75-76, because scanned is incremented at line 107 before scan() is called. Both halves of the claim are exactly true.
verdicts.what_i_tried_to_refute_it_with: FP-01 and FP-08 (GitHub secret scanning with push protection as the compensating control): correctly UNKNOWN — governance.json:39-44 is a desired-state declaration that flags its own '_unverified_availability': true, and no exported setting exists, so the control cannot be answered as present. FP-02 (value not attacker-controlled): does not apply; the suppressed token is precisely a value nobody constrained. FP-07 (data has no security value): fails — a live credential is the definition of security-relevant. FP-09 (construct is not what it looks like): I checked whether BENIGN might be applied to the token elsewhere; it is not, line 84 is the only application and it takes `line`. I also found one inaccuracy the finding did not claim: the summary string says 'file(s) outside bench/cases' while `scanned` is incremented for bench files too.
verdicts.severity_assessment: agree with severity `low` — the detector is a second line and no attacker chooses what gets committed. But the STATUS is under-called: `hardening` is defined as 'no weakness was demonstrated and none is claimed', and this finding both claims an evasion and carries confidence: high, which I have now demonstrated with a test. By this vocabulary's own criteria it is `confirmed`, severity `low`. Filing a demonstrated, reproducible control bypass as `hardening` understates it in the deliverable and, in a corpus that counts statuses, distorts the measurement.
verdicts.checked: Read scripts/gates/lib/secret_scan.py in full and scripts/gates/lib/common.sh:6-12 for the exit-code doctrine it cites. Ran a copy of the scanner in a scratch directory over six synthetic files (four text cases with a fabricated AWS-format key, one 2.4 MB oversized file, one undecodable binary) and captured both the FINDING lines emitted and the 'measured: 6 file(s)' summary against the six files actually present.
verdicts.not_checked: I did not test every pattern in PATTERNS against the BENIGN regex, only aws-access-key-id and private-key-block. I did not exercise the bench/cases branch at lines 116-142 or the answer-key path. No real credential was used, and git history was not scanned — so, as the finding says, this establishes a defect in a detector and nothing about whether anything leaked.
